old_caption: The video captures a scene set against a completely black background, emphasizing the stark contrast and the dynamic movement of the objects within the frame. The primary focus is on several shards of glass suspended in mid-air, appearing to be in motion. These shards vary in size and shape, with some being larger and more jagged, while others are smaller and smoother. As the video progresses, these glass fragments move downward, suggesting they have been thrown or broken from an unseen source above. The movement is fluid and continuous, creating a sense of urgency and tension. The black backdrop enhances the visibility of the glass shards, making them stand out prominently. There are no other objects or characters present in the scene, which keeps the viewer's attention solely on the falling glass pieces. The overall atmosphere is one of suspense and anticipation, as the viewer wonders about the origin of the glass and what might happen next.

caption: The video captures several translucent, sharp-edged shards suspended in a near-black void, lit from one side so their thin edges glow pale blue-green. A large shard hangs pinned at the top-right corner, holding its position and silhouette unchanged throughout, serving as a fixed reference against which the other motion is read. Below it, a smaller elongated shard drifts steadily downward from the upper-middle of the frame toward the center, its outline tilting and rotating as it tumbles through the descent. Along the bottom edge, a loose cluster of additional shards creeps slowly downward, with the leftmost fragment gradually slipping out of view while the others remain near the lower border. Fine dust specks scatter across the darkness, shifting slightly relative to the stationary top-right piece, suggesting a slow drift of the particulate field. No impact or release is shown. The falling is already underway in the first frame and continues past the last. The central shard is still descending and turning when the excerpt ends, its motion unbroken and continuous.

necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
